summary: POP affinity migration causing cold KV cache warm-up and persistent tail latency
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC, NimbleChat reported elevated tail latency (p99) and intermittent timeouts for requests routed to their dedicated pool. Pattern correlates with our POP affinity migration which moved a subset of NimbleChat traffic from SFO POP to PHX POP. Impact: increased p95/p99 token latency (p99 rose from ~1.1s to ~3.8s) and ~0.7% 5xx/timeouts on user-facing generate endpoints for NimbleChat traffic. Timeline: 08:05 UTC - automated migration triggered; 08:12 UTC - first customer report; 08:20 UTC - alerts fired on routing and p99; 09:00 UTC - Support engaged SRE and routing team. Environment: prod, NimbleChat dedicated pool, us-west-2 region (primary), backup in eu-west-1 for some accounts. Steps to reproduce: 1) Hit /v1/generate with NimbleChat API key pinned to dedicated pool from an us-west client IP that resolves to the new PHX POP via routing table. 2) Observe initial request p50~300ms but p99 outliers >=3s after a period of sustained traffic. Observed behavior: high initial TTFB on cold requests after migration; sustained elevated p99 during early hours after migration; logs show increased KV cache miss rate on PHX nodes for NimbleChat account, and backend shows more frequent model weight page-in activity for first few tens of requests. Hypothesis: POP affinity migration caused a portion of cached KV prefixes and runtime warm state to be unavailable in the new POP. The serving runtime relies on prefix/KV cache warmness to keep per-token latencies low; when affinity changes, many sessions are redirected to nodes with cold KV and cold GPU kernels causing page-in/serialization overhead and higher kernel select overhead, producing tail latency. Additional factor: NAT SNAT pools and connection multiplexing differences in PHX appear to increase TCP handshake variance for some client subnets. Investigation notes: - Confirmed KV cache miss rate for NimbleChat namespace increased from ~2% to ~38% immediately post-migration (logs: kv-store.metrics:miss_rate). - GPU profiling on PHX nodes shows elevated kernel compile/selection calls in first 30s of new sessions. - TCP SYN retransmits rose for ~3% of client IPs routed to PHX due to different egress path MTU handling (pcap snapshots). - Routing config shows split-horizon weight change applied at 08:05 UTC (rbac note: migration job id migr-2026-03-10-08). Priority/impact rationale: Dedicated customer experiencing production regressions; P1 until warm-up completes and mitigation applied. Next steps: 1) Roll back partial affinity weights to SFO for affected account to restore cache locality (done 2026-03-10 09:45 UTC). 2) Trigger targeted KV cache pre-warm for NimbleChat prefixes in PHX nodes (planned 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC). 3) Apply a temporary routing-steering hold on any automated POP migrations for dedicated pools until we have pre-warm in place. 4) Network team to validate SNAT pool MTU and connection multiplexing settings for PHX (ticket INT-442). 5) Monitor p95/p99 and KV miss rate for 24 hours and alert if p99 > 2s. Mitigation timeline and current state: rollback performed reduced p99 to ~1.3s but not back to baseline; targeted pre-warm scheduled. This ticket tracks follow-up work and customer updates.

investigation_notes: KV store metrics show namespace nimblechat-prod miss_rate spiked to 38% immediately after migration and decayed to ~6% after rollback and partial pre-warm.
GPU runtime probes indicate first-connection kernel selection/compilation overhead accounted for ~30-40% of p99 regression on cold sessions.
PHX egress path had differing MTU/fragmentation behavior for a subset of client subnets causing increased SYN-RTX in ~3% of flows.
No model version mismatch found; pinned model hashes identical across POPs.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: Rolled back POP affinity weights for NimbleChat to previous SFO POP at 2026-03-10 09:45 UTC which reduced p99 from ~3.8s to ~1.3s.
Medium-term mitigation: Implement targeted KV pre-warm for customer namespaces in destination POPs prior to affinity cutover. Pre-warm run initiated 2026-03-11.

Long-term: Add pre-migration warmup step to migration runbook and add monitoring-based gating for automated POP migrations for dedicated customers. Routing and infra teams assigned follow-up (INT-442 for networking validation, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/274 for runbook changes).
Customer follow-up: Schedule postmortem meeting with NimbleChat for 2026-03-13 to review timeline, impact, and compensatory credits if applicable.
